Reusable, versioned, checksummed tasks for coding agents — run with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Antigravity. Search → inspect → approve → execute, with a log of everything that ran.

The whole idea in 30 seconds: find a package, ask an agent what it would do, review the approval prompt (checksum, parameters, tool grants), let your agent execute it, and see the run land in your history. The output above is replayed from a real recorded session (docs/demo/).

A Clawx package is a markdown file with YAML front matter. The front matter declares metadata — name, version, typed parameters, dependencies, the tools the package wants. The body becomes the system prompt of an agent CLI. "Installing" a package means: fetch it from a registry, verify its SHA256 against the index, show an approval prompt, execute it under the agent you chose, and append the outcome to an execution log. There is no code generation and no compilation — the install is a governed agent invocation.

Warning

Security model — read this before running packages.

A package is a prompt executed by an agent with real tool access on your machine. Treat running one with the same suspicion as curl | sh.

  • allowed_tools is enforced at the subprocess boundary only under the claude provider, where it is forwarded as --allowedTools. Under codex, opencode, gemini, and agy it is disclosure in the approval prompt, not a Clawx-enforced boundary — those CLIs govern tool access through their own sandboxing and approval modes.
  • SHA256 verification proves the file you run is byte-identical to what the registry indexed. It says nothing about whether those bytes are safe. A registry is a trust root: only add registries you trust, and use clawx info to have a tool-less agent summarize a package before running it.
  • Agents are not deterministic and can misinterpret instructions. The approval prompt and the execution log exist to bound and audit that risk, not to eliminate it.

Why not shell scripts?

Fair question — it's the first one everybody asks. A shell script encodes a mechanism: the exact commands that worked on the machines its author anticipated. A Clawx package encodes intent — the goal, the constraints, the verification steps — and the agent picks the mechanism for the machine in front of it. The same dockerize package containerizes a Go, Node, or Python repo because it detects the ecosystem instead of assuming it; a script would need a case statement per ecosystem, per package manager, per layout, and it still breaks on the repo its author never saw.

On top of that, packages carry infrastructure scripts never accumulated:

  • Typed parameters — declared in front matter with defaults; missing required ones are prompted for, not discovered as an unbound variable at runtime.
  • Dependencies — depends_on resolves transitively against your registries and installs first.
  • Provider portability — one package runs under claude, codex, opencode, gemini, or agy; switching agents is an env var, not a rewrite.
  • A governed run — SHA256 verification against the registry index, then an approval prompt listing the tools, env vars, and parameter values before anything executes.
  • An execution trail — every run appends package, version, SHA, exit code, and duration to ~/.clawx/execution.log. You can answer "what ran on this machine, when, and did it succeed?"

And the honest counterpoint: an agent run is slower than a script and not deterministic — the same package produces a different transcript each time. If your task is fully mechanical, keep the shell script (a package can simply call it). Clawx is for the judgment-shaped tasks where scripts rot: auditing, migrating, configuring against whatever the repository actually contains.

How it compares

Candidly: if the task is deterministic, a script or Makefile is strictly better. If you manage fleets of machines toward a desired state, that's Ansible. Agent skills are the closest cousin — but they're tied to a single agent product and ship without versioned distribution, checksums, approval gates, or an execution log. Prompt libraries share text; nothing fetches, verifies, executes, or records it. Clawx occupies the gap: distributable, verifiable, auditable tasks that need judgment at runtime.

Showcase

The packages that show what the model is for — multi-step, context-aware work, not brew install with extra steps:

go-modernize — audit an aging Go repo: toolchain drift, deprecated APIs (ioutil, strings.Title, ...), idiom drift, outdated deps, vet/lint. Writes a risk-grouped MODERNIZE.md; with -p apply=true it applies the mechanical fixes and proves build and tests stay green (it refuses to touch a dirty working tree, and reverts anything that breaks). This is the package in the demo above.

clawx run go-modernize                    # report only
clawx run go-modernize -p apply=true      # apply safe fixes, re-verify

ci-baseline — detect the ecosystem, then set up the three layers everyone postpones: a linter config, a GitHub Actions workflow running the repo's actual build/test/lint commands, and pre-commit hooks (pre-commit or lefthook). Respects anything that already exists, runs the linter once, and tells you whether the first CI run will be green.

clawx run ci-baseline -p hook_manager=lefthook

docker-image-diet — build your image, rank its layers, rewrite the Dockerfile (multi-stage split, slimmer base, cache hygiene, .dockerignore), rebuild, and report before/after sizes from real builds. If it can't make the image smaller, it restores the original and says so.

clawx run docker-image-diet

Alongside those: repo-security-review, setup-github-actions, dockerfile-audit, migrate-eslint-config, prepare-open-source-release, and 350+ more install, setup, audit, and scaffolding packages in the built-in registry.

Install

Install the latest release with one command (macOS and Linux):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debarshibasak/clawx/master/install.sh | sh

The script detects your platform, verifies the archive against the release's checksums.txt, and installs to /usr/local/bin (falling back to ~/.local/bin). Pin a version with CLAWX_VERSION=v0.2.1 or change the destination with CLAWX_INSTALL_DIR. From a checkout, make install-latest runs the same script.

Archives for darwin/linux (amd64, arm64) and windows/amd64 ship with every release, alongside a checksums.txt — grab one manually from the releases page if you prefer.

Windows (PowerShell)

The Windows archive is named clawx_<tag>_windows_amd64.tar.gz. In PowerShell, download it with the matching checksums.txt, verify the SHA256, and put clawx.exe in a directory on your user PATH:

$tag = "v0.2.1" # replace with the release tag you downloaded
$archive = "clawx_${tag}_windows_amd64.tar.gz"
$base = "https://github.com/debarshibasak/clawx/releases/download/$tag"

Invoke-WebRequest "$base/$archive" -OutFile ".\$archive"
Invoke-WebRequest "$base/checksums.txt" -OutFile .\checksums.txt
$expected = Get-Content .\checksums.txt |
  Where-Object { $_ -match "\s$([regex]::Escape($archive))$" } |
  ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "\s+")[0] } |
  Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $expected) { throw "No checksum found for $archive" }
$actual = (Get-FileHash ".\$archive" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected.ToLowerInvariant()) { throw "SHA256 verification failed" }

tar -xzf ".\$archive"
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $installDir | Out-Null
Move-Item -Force .\clawx.exe (Join-Path $installDir "clawx.exe")
$userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
$pathEntries = @($userPath -split ";" | Where-Object { $_ })
if ($pathEntries -notcontains $installDir) {
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", (($pathEntries + $installDir) -join ";"), "User")
}
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"
clawx --help

PowerShell stores Clawx state under %USERPROFILE%\.clawx (the equivalent of ~/.clawx on macOS/Linux). clawx list uses $env:PAGER when stdout is a terminal and falls back to more; use clawx list --no-pager or set $env:CLAWX_NO_PAGER = "1" for non-interactive output.

WSL is a separate environment: a Linux Clawx binary uses the Linux home directory (~/.clawx) and Linux provider CLIs. A Windows binary launched from PowerShell uses %USERPROFILE%\.clawx and needs the selected provider CLI on the Windows PATH; the two environments do not share state automatically.

Or build from source:

go build -o clawx .      # or: make build
go install .             # or: make install

Clawx shells out to an agent CLI, so you need one of claude, codex, opencode, gemini or agy on your PATH. The default is claude; select another with CLAWX_PROVIDER.

Shell completion

The completion command is generated by Cobra. After installing clawx, use the setup for your shell below and start a new shell (or source the generated file) to enable tab completion.

Bash

For bash-completion v2, install the generated function in the user completion directory:

mkdir -p "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}"
clawx completion bash > "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}/clawx"

On systems without bash-completion, source a file from your shell startup instead:

clawx completion bash > "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"
printf '\nsource "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"\n' >> "$HOME/.bashrc"
source "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"

Zsh

For the stock macOS zsh, keep the completion function in a user directory and add that directory to fpath:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.zsh/completions"
clawx completion zsh > "$HOME/.zsh/completions/_clawx"
printf '\nfpath=("$HOME/.zsh/completions" $fpath)\nautoload -Uz compinit && compinit\n' >> "$HOME/.zshrc"
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit

If zsh was installed with Homebrew, use its site-functions directory instead (/opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon, /usr/local on Intel):

zsh_site="$(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions"
mkdir -p "$zsh_site"
clawx completion zsh > "$zsh_site/_clawx"
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit

Fish

Fish loads completion files from this directory automatically in new shells:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/fish/completions"
clawx completion fish > "$HOME/.config/fish/completions/clawx.fish"

Install clawx with clawx

Already have clawx? It updates itself the way it runs everything else — the built-in registry ships an install-clawx package that fetches the latest release, verifies its checksum, and installs the binary:

clawx run install-clawx

Like every run, it goes through the approval prompt first, and the execution is logged to ~/.clawx/execution.log.

Quickstart

Clawx ships with a built-in default registry (the registry/ directory of this repo served over GitHub raw), so it works with no setup:

clawx list                        # browse the catalog
clawx search docker               # find packages by name/description
clawx info go-modernize           # what would this package do?
clawx run go-modernize            # fetch, verify, approve, execute
clawx history                     # what has run on this machine?
clawx rolladice                   # what should I run next?

clawx help prints the full guide — commands, package format, security model, environment variables and local state.

Watching a package run

By default a run prints one live progress line — elapsed time, todo completion and the current tool call — and stays quiet otherwise:

⠹ claude · 12s · todos 1/4 · 3 tool calls · Bash: go vet ./...

Pass --verbose (or set CLAWX_VERBOSE=1) to stream the agent's narrative, its tool calls and its todo list as they happen:

$ clawx run go-modernize --verbose

Baseline is green (build ✅, tests ✅). Auditing the source now.
→ Bash: go vet ./...
── todos ──
  [x] Establish build/test baseline
  [>] Audit for deprecated APIs
  [ ] Write MODERNIZE.md

The agent's final summary is shown only in verbose mode.

Commands

Command Signature Does
add clawx add <url> [--server] [--name] [--ref] Register a registry: a git repo (default) or a clawx HTTP server.
list clawx list [--refresh] [--no-pager] List packages across every configured registry, paged through $PAGER when printed to a terminal.
search clawx search <term> [term...] [--refresh] Search packages by name and description; multiple terms must all match.
run clawx run <name>[@version] [-p k=v] [--prompt] [--verbose] [-y] Fetch, verify, approve, execute. The critical path. Aliased as install.
info clawx info <name> [--no-summary] Package metadata, plus a tool-less agent summary of what it would do.
rolladice clawx rolladice [--fast] [--dir] [--no-agent] [--limit] Scan your workspace and the registries, recommend what to install next.
uninstall clawx uninstall <name> [-y] Drop the install record from local state.
update clawx update [name] Re-fetch packages, reinstall when the SHA or version changed.
history clawx history [--limit] Replay the NDJSON execution log.
pipeline clawx pipeline <pipeline.yaml> [--dry-run] Execute a multi-step pipeline of packages in sequence. clawx run <file.yaml> does the same.
server clawx server --dir <path> [--port] Run the registry HTTP server. index.yaml is built at request time.

clawx rolladice

Rolls the dice on what to install next. It scans the current directory for projects (ecosystem manifests), libraries (parsed out of those manifests), containers (Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes, Helm, devcontainer) and notable files (CI, IaC, build, test, lint, data, docs) — then matches all of that against the catalogs served by your registries.

  Detected:
    [*] go                 go.mod (github.com/acme/svc)
    [*] dockerfile         Dockerfile
    [*] kubernetes         deploy/app.yaml
    [*] ci:github-actions  .github/workflows/ci.yml

  Roll:

    1. base-setup               v1.0.0     score 72
       Prepare a Go service repository with linting and CI
       - required by installed analytics
       - matches your workspace: go, ci
       clawx run base-setup

Ranking is deterministic and runs offline: unmet dependencies of installed packages outrank packages that build on installed ones, which outrank workspace-signal and shared-vocabulary matches. The shortlist is then handed to the agent, which explains the picks — a read-only call with no tools granted.

  • --fast skips both the workspace walk and the agent, ranking purely from what you already have installed. It returns in milliseconds.
  • --no-agent prints the offline shortlist without invoking any agent.

Only manifest files are ever opened. .env files and your source files are recorded by path and never read.

Package format

YAML front matter delimited by ---, followed by the markdown body that becomes the agent's system prompt. Only name is required.

---
name: setup-project
version: 1.0.0
description: Scaffold a new project directory
author: adaptive-scale
author_email: team@adaptive.live
allowed_tools:
  - bash
env_required: []
depends_on: []
params:
  - name: project_name
    type: string          # string | int | bool
    required: true
    description: Directory to create
  - name: language
    type: string
    required: false
    default: go
---

You are a project scaffolding assistant. Use the Input Parameters provided to…

depends_on packages are resolved transitively and installed first, non-interactively. Fixtures live in testdata/packages/.

Want to write one? Create your first Clawx package in five minutes walks through template → local test → pull request, with a real transcript.

Add a custom registry

  • git (default) — clawx add github.com/owner/repo [--ref main]. The repo is cloned under ~/.clawx/cache/repos/ and the index is built from its *.md files.
  • server — clawx add http://host:8080 --server. Any clawx server instance, which builds index.yaml by scanning its --dir at request time.

To try the server flavor against the bundled fixtures:

./clawx server --dir ./testdata/packages --port 8080   # terminal 1

./clawx add http://localhost:8080 --server             # terminal 2
./clawx list
./clawx run hello-world

Indexes are cached on disk with a TTL (default 1h); --refresh bypasses it. Opt out of the built-in default registry with CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1.

Providers

The agent CLI sits behind a Provider interface selected by CLAWX_PROVIDER.

Provider Invocation allowed_tools
claude (default) --system-prompt-file <tmp> Forwarded as --allowedTools — enforced at the subprocess boundary.
codex codex exec -, prompt via stdin Not forwarded; governed by Codex's own approval/sandbox modes.
opencode opencode run, prompt via stdin Not forwarded; governed by OpenCode's own config.
gemini system prompt via GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD=<tmp>, user prompt via -p Not forwarded; governed by Gemini CLI's approval modes and settings.
agy agy -p <prompt> (Antigravity CLI; alias: antigravity) Not forwarded; governed by agy's own permission prompts.

This is the asymmetry the warning at the top of this README is about: allowed_tools is a real security boundary only under claude. Everywhere else it is disclosure shown in the approval prompt.

clawx info and clawx rolladice are the exceptions — both are read-only calls whose system prompt forbids tool use, and under claude no --allowedTools flag is passed at all.

Environment

Variable Effect
CLAWX_PROVIDER Agent CLI: claude (default), codex, opencode, gemini, agy.
CLAWX_PROVIDER_BIN Absolute path to the agent binary, bypassing PATH lookup.
CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1 Don't inject the built-in default registry.
CLAWX_INSTALL_IDS=1 Generate and persist a UUID per install.
CLAWX_VERBOSE=1 Stream agent output as if --verbose was passed.
CLAWX_NO_PAGER=1 Never page clawx list output, even on a terminal.
PAGER Pager used by clawx list (default: less -FRX, then more).

Local state

Everything persisted lives under ~/.clawx/:

config.json        registries + cache TTL
cache/<sha>.json   cached registry indexes
cache/repos/       cloned git-backed registries
installed.json     install records
execution.log      NDJSON execution history

Contributing

The easiest contribution doesn't require reading any Go: write a package. Start with Create your first Clawx package in five minutes, then look at the good first issue label. CONTRIBUTING.md covers the codebase itself, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains how the pieces fit, and ROADMAP.md is where the project is headed. Security reports go through SECURITY.md.

Development

make build     # go build -o clawx .
make test      # go test ./...
make vet       # go vet ./...
make fmt       # gofmt -s -w .
make smoke     # serve ./testdata/packages on :8080

In PowerShell, download it with the matching checksums.txt, verify the SHA256, and put clawx.exe in a directory on your user PATH: $tag = "v0.2.1" # replace with the release tag you downloaded $archive = "clawx_${tag}_windows_amd64.tar.gz" $base = "https://github.com/debarshibasak/clawx/releases/download/$tag" Invoke-WebRequest "$base/$archive" -OutFile ".\$archive" Invoke-WebRequest "$base/checksums.txt" -OutFile .\checksums.txt $expected = Get-Content .\checksums.txt | Where-Object { $_ -match "\s$([regex]::Escape($archive))$" } | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "\s+")[0] } | Select-Object -First 1 if (-not $expected) { throw "No checksum found for $archive" } $actual = (Get-FileHash ".\$archive" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() if ($actual -ne $expected.ToLowerInvariant()) { throw "SHA256 verification failed" } tar -xzf ".\$archive" $installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "bin" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $installDir | Out-Null Move-Item -Force .\clawx.exe (Join-Path $installDir "clawx.exe") $userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User") $pathEntries = @($userPath -split ";" | Where-Object { $_ }) if ($pathEntries -notcontains $installDir) { [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", (($pathEntries + $installDir) -join ";"), "User") } $env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path" clawx --help PowerShell stores Clawx state under %USERPROFILE%\.clawx (the equivalent of ~/.clawx on macOS/Linux). clawx list uses $env:PAGER when stdout is a terminal and falls back to more; use clawx list --no-pager or set $env:CLAWX_NO_PAGER = "1" for non-interactive output. WSL is a separate environment: a Linux Clawx binary uses the Linux home directory (~/.clawx) and Linux provider CLIs. A Windows binary launched from PowerShell uses %USERPROFILE%\.clawx and needs the selected provider CLI on the Windows PATH; the two environments do not share state automatically. Or build from source: go build -o clawx . # or: make build go install . # or: make install Clawx shells out to an agent CLI, so you need one of claude, codex, opencode, gemini or agy on your PATH. The default is claude; select another with CLAWX_PROVIDER. Shell completion The completion command is generated by Cobra. After installing clawx, use the setup for your shell below and start a new shell (or source the generated file) to enable tab completion. Bash For bash-completion v2, install the generated function in the user completion directory: mkdir -p "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}" clawx completion bash > "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}/clawx" On systems without bash-completion, source a file from your shell startup instead: clawx completion bash > "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash" printf '
source "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"
' >> "$HOME/.bashrc" source "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash" Zsh For the stock macOS zsh, keep the completion function in a user directory and add that directory to fpath: mkdir -p "$HOME/.zsh/completions" clawx completion zsh > "$HOME/.zsh/completions/_clawx" printf '
fpath=("$HOME/.zsh/completions" $fpath)
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit
' >> "$HOME/.zshrc" autoload -Uz compinit && compinit If zsh was installed with Homebrew, use its site-functions directory instead (/opt/homebrew on Apple Silicon, /usr/local on Intel): zsh_site="$(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions" mkdir -p "$zsh_site" clawx completion zsh > "$zsh_site/_clawx" autoload -Uz compinit && compinit Fish Fish loads completion files from this directory automatically in new shells: mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/fish/completions" clawx completion fish > "$HOME/.config/fish/completions/clawx.fish" Install clawx with clawx Already have clawx? It updates itself the way it runs everything else — the built-in registry ships an install-clawx package that fetches the latest release, verifies its checksum, and installs the binary: clawx run install-clawx Like every run, it goes through the approval prompt first, and the execution is logged to ~/.clawx/execution.log. Quickstart Clawx ships with a built-in default registry (the registry/ directory of this repo served over GitHub raw), so it works with no setup: clawx list # browse the catalog clawx search docker # find packages by name/description clawx info go-modernize # what would this package do? clawx run go-modernize # fetch, verify, approve, execute clawx history # what has run on this machine? clawx rolladice # what should I run next? clawx help prints the full guide — commands, package format, security model, environment variables and local state. Watching a package run By default a run prints one live progress line — elapsed time, todo completion and the current tool call — and stays quiet otherwise: ⠹ claude · 12s · todos 1/4 · 3 tool calls · Bash: go vet ./... Pass --verbose (or set CLAWX_VERBOSE=1) to stream the agent's narrative, its tool calls and its todo list as they happen: $ clawx run go-modernize --verbose Baseline is green (build ✅, tests ✅). Auditing the source now. → Bash: go vet ./... ── todos ── [x] Establish build/test baseline [>] Audit for deprecated APIs [ ] Write MODERNIZE.md The agent's final summary is shown only in verbose mode. Commands Command Signature Does add clawx add <url> [--server] [--name] [--ref] Register a registry: a git repo (default) or a clawx HTTP server. list clawx list [--refresh] [--no-pager] List packages across every configured registry, paged through $PAGER when printed to a terminal. search clawx search <term> [term...] [--refresh] Search packages by name and description; multiple terms must all match. run clawx run <name>[@version] [-p k=v] [--prompt] [--verbose] [-y] Fetch, verify, approve, execute. The critical path. Aliased as install. info clawx info <name> [--no-summary] Package metadata, plus a tool-less agent summary of what it would do. rolladice clawx rolladice [--fast] [--dir] [--no-agent] [--limit] Scan your workspace and the registries, recommend what to install next. uninstall clawx uninstall <name> [-y] Drop the install record from local state. update clawx update [name] Re-fetch packages, reinstall when the SHA or version changed. history clawx history [--limit] Replay the NDJSON execution log. pipeline clawx pipeline <pipeline.yaml> [--dry-run] Execute a multi-step pipeline of packages in sequence. clawx run <file.yaml> does the same. server clawx server --dir <path> [--port] Run the registry HTTP server. index.yaml is built at request time. clawx rolladice Rolls the dice on what to install next. It scans the current directory for projects (ecosystem manifests), libraries (parsed out of those manifests), containers (Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes, Helm, devcontainer) and notable files (CI, IaC, build, test, lint, data, docs) — then matches all of that against the catalogs served by your registries. Detected: [*] go go.mod (github.com/acme/svc) [*] dockerfile Dockerfile [*] kubernetes deploy/app.yaml [*] ci:github-actions .github/workflows/ci.yml Roll: 1. base-setup v1.0.0 score 72 Prepare a Go service repository with linting and CI - required by installed analytics - matches your workspace: go, ci clawx run base-setup Ranking is deterministic and runs offline: unmet dependencies of installed packages outrank packages that build on installed ones, which outrank workspace-signal and shared-vocabulary matches. The shortlist is then handed to the agent, which explains the picks — a read-only call with no tools granted. --fast skips both the workspace walk and the agent, ranking purely from what you already have installed. It returns in milliseconds. --no-agent prints the offline shortlist without invoking any agent. Only manifest files are ever opened. .env files and your source files are recorded by path and never read. Package format YAML front matter delimited by ---, followed by the markdown body that becomes the agent's system prompt. Only name is required. --- name: setup-project version: 1.0.0 description: Scaffold a new project directory author: adaptive-scale author_email: team@adaptive.live allowed_tools: - bash env_required: [] depends_on: [] params: - name: project_name type: string # string | int | bool required: true description: Directory to create - name: language type: string required: false default: go --- You are a project scaffolding assistant. Use the Input Parameters provided to… depends_on packages are resolved transitively and installed first, non-interactively. Fixtures live in testdata/packages/. Want to write one? Create your first Clawx package in five minutes walks through template → local test → pull request, with a real transcript. Add a custom registry git (default) — clawx add github.com/owner/repo [--ref main]. The repo is cloned under ~/.clawx/cache/repos/ and the index is built from its *.md files. server — clawx add http://host:8080 --server. Any clawx server instance, which builds index.yaml by scanning its --dir at request time. To try the server flavor against the bundled fixtures: ./clawx server --dir ./testdata/packages --port 8080 # terminal 1 ./clawx add http://localhost:8080 --server # terminal 2 ./clawx list ./clawx run hello-world Indexes are cached on disk with a TTL (default 1h); --refresh bypasses it. Opt out of the built-in default registry with CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1. Providers The agent CLI sits behind a Provider interface selected by CLAWX_PROVIDER. Provider Invocation allowed_tools claude (default) --system-prompt-file <tmp> Forwarded as --allowedTools — enforced at the subprocess boundary. codex codex exec -, prompt via stdin Not forwarded; governed by Codex's own approval/sandbox modes. opencode opencode run, prompt via stdin Not forwarded; governed by OpenCode's own config. gemini system prompt via GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD=<tmp>, user prompt via -p Not forwarded; governed by Gemini CLI's approval modes and settings. agy agy -p <prompt> (Antigravity CLI; alias: antigravity) Not forwarded; governed by agy's own permission prompts. This is the asymmetry the warning at the top of this README is about: allowed_tools is a real security boundary only under claude. Everywhere else it is disclosure shown in the approval prompt. clawx info and clawx rolladice are the exceptions — both are read-only calls whose system prompt forbids tool use, and under claude no --allowedTools flag is passed at all. Environment Variable Effect CLAWX_PROVIDER Agent CLI: claude (default), codex, opencode, gemini, agy. CLAWX_PROVIDER_BIN Absolute path to the agent binary, bypassing PATH lookup. CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1 Don't inject the built-in default registry. CLAWX_INSTALL_IDS=1 Generate and persist a UUID per install. CLAWX_VERBOSE=1 Stream agent output as if --verbose was passed. CLAWX_NO_PAGER=1 Never page clawx list output, even on a terminal. PAGER Pager used by clawx list (default: less -FRX, then more). Local state Everything persisted lives under ~/.clawx/: config.json registries + cache TTL cache/<sha>.json cached registry indexes cache/repos/ cloned git-backed registries installed.json install records execution.log NDJSON execution history Contributing The easiest contribution doesn't require reading any Go: write a package. Start with Create your first Clawx package in five minutes, then look at the good first issue label. CONTRIBUTING.md covers the codebase itself, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains how the pieces fit, and ROADMAP.md is where the project is headed. Security reports go through SECURITY.md. blocks.html_en: Fair question — it's the first one everybody asks. A shell script encodes a mechanism: the exact commands that worked on the machines its author anticipated. A Clawx package encodes intent — the goal, the constraints, the verification steps — and the agent picks the mechanism for the machine in front of it. The same dockerize package containerizes a Go, Node, or Python repo because it detects the ecosystem instead of assuming it; a script would need a case statement per ecosystem, per package manager, per layout, and it still breaks on the repo its author never saw.

blocks.html_en: Candidly: if the task is deterministic, a script or Makefile is strictly better. If you manage fleets of machines toward a desired state, that's Ansible. Agent skills are the closest cousin — but they're tied to a single agent product and ship without versioned distribution, checksums, approval gates, or an execution log. 编码代理的可重用、版本化、校验和任务 - 使用 Claude Code、Codex、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 或 Antigravity 运行。 搜索→检查→批准→执行，并记录运行的所有内容。

30 秒内完成整个想法：找到一个包，询问代理它将做什么，查看批准提示（校验和、参数、工具授权），让您的代理执行它，并在您的历史记录中查看运行情况。 上面的输出是从真实录制的会话（docs/demo/）重播的。

Clawx 包是一个带有 YAML 开头内容的 Markdown 文件。 前面的内容声明了元数据——名称、版本、类型参数、依赖项、包所需的工具。 正文成为代理 CLI 的系统提示符。 “安装”包意味着：从注册表中获取它，根据索引验证其 SHA256，显示批准提示，在您选择的代理下执行它，并将结果附加到执行日志中。 没有代码生成，也没有编译——安装是受管理的代理调用。

警告

安全模型 - 在运行包之前阅读此内容。

包是由在您的计算机上具有实际工具访问权限的代理执行的提示。 像curl一样对待运行一个|嘘。

  • allowed_tools 仅在 claude 提供程序下在子进程边界强制执行，在此处它作为 --allowedTools 转发。 在 codex、opencode、gemini 和 agy 下，它是在批准提示中披露，而不是 Clawx 强制的边界 - 这些 CLI 通过自己的沙箱和批准模式来管理工具访问。
  • SHA256 验证证明您运行的文件与注册表索引的文件在字节上相同。 它没有说明这些字节是否安全。 注册表是一个信任根：仅添加您信任的注册表，并使用clawx信息让无工具代理在运行包之前对其进行汇总。
  • 代理不是确定性的，可能会误解指令。 批准提示和执行日志的存在是为了限制和审核该风险，而不是消除它。

为什么不使用 shell 脚本呢？

公平的问题——这是每个人问的第一个问题。 shell 脚本编码一种机制：在其作者预期的机器上运行的确切命令。 Clawx 包对意图（目标、约束、验证步骤）进行编码，然后代理为其前面的机器选择机制。 同一个 dockerize 包容器化了 Go、Node 或 Python 存储库，因为它检测生态系统而不是假设它；一个脚本需要每个生态系统、每个包管理器、每个布局都有一个 case 语句，并且它仍然会在其作者从未见过的存储库上崩溃。

最重要的是，包携带从未积累的基础设施脚本：

  • 类型化参数——在前面声明并使用默认值；缺少必需的变量会被提示，而不是在运行时作为未绑定变量被发现。
  • 依赖关系——depends_on 根据您的注册表传递解析并首先安装。
  • 提供者可移植性——一个包在 claude、codex、opencode、gemini 或 agy 下运行；切换代理是一个环境变量，而不是重写。
  • 受管控的运行 - 针对注册表索引进行 SHA256 验证，然后在执行任何操作之前出现批准提示，列出工具、环境变量和参数值。
  • 执行跟踪 - 每次运行都会将包、版本、SHA、退出代码和持续时间附加到 ~/.clawx/execution.log。 您可以回答“这台机器上运行了什么，何时运行，是否成功？”

诚实的对立面是：代理运行比脚本慢并且不确定 - 相同的包每次都会生成不同的转录本。 如果您的任务是完全机械的，请保留 shell 脚本（包可以简单地调用它）。 Clawx 适用于脚本失效的判断型任务：针对存储库实际包含的内容进行审核、迁移、配置。

坦率地说：如果任务是确定性的，那么脚本或 Makefile 绝对更好。 如果您管理机器群以达到所需的状态，那就是 Ansible。 代理技能是最接近的，但它们与单个代理产品相关联，并且没有版本化分发、校验和、批准门或执行日志。 提示图书馆共享文本；没有任何东西获取、验证、执行或记录它。 Clawx 填补了空白：可分发、可验证、可审计的任务，需要在运行时进行判断。

展示柜

显示模型用途的软件包 — 多步骤、上下文感知工作，而不是通过额外步骤进行安装：

go-modernize — 审核老化的 Go 存储库：工具链漂移、已弃用的 API（ioutil、strings.Title 等）、习惯用法漂移、过时的 deps、vet/lint。 编写风险分组的 MODERNIZE.md；使用 -p apply=true 它会应用机械修复并证明构建和测试保持绿色（它拒绝接触肮脏的工作树，并恢复任何损坏的东西）。 这是上面演示中的包。

clawx run go-modernize                    # report only
clawx run go-modernize -p apply=true      # apply safe fixes, re-verify

ci-baseline — 检测生态系统，然后设置每个人都推迟的三层：linter 配置、运行存储库的实际构建/测试/lint 命令的 GitHub Actions 工作流程以及预提交挂钩（预提交或 lefthook）。 尊重已经存在的任何内容，运行 linter 一次，并告诉您第一次 CI 运行是否会是绿色的。

clawx run ci-baseline -p hook_manager=lefthook

docker-image-diet — 构建镜像、对其层进行排名、重写 Dockerfile（多阶段分割、更精简的基础、缓存卫生、.dockerignore）、重建并报告实际构建之前/之后的大小。 如果它不能使图像变小，它就会恢复原始图像并这样说。

clawx run docker-image-diet

除此之外：repo-security-review、setup-github-actions、dockerfile-audit、migrate-eslint-config、prepare-open-source-release 以及内置注册表中的 350 多个安装、设置、审核和脚手架包。

安装

使用一个命令安装最新版本（macOS 和 Linux）：

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debarshibasak/clawx/master/install.sh | sh

该脚本会检测您的平台，根据版本的 checksums.txt 验证存档，然后安装到 /usr/local/bin （回退到 ~/.local/bin）。 使用 CLAWX_VERSION=v0.2.1 固定版本，或使用 CLAWX_INSTALL_DIR 更改目标。 从结帐中， make install-latest 运行相同的脚本。

每个版本都会附带 darwin/linux（amd64、arm64）和 windows/amd64 的存档，以及 checksums.txt — 如果您愿意，可以从版本页面手动获取一个。

Windows（PowerShell）

Windows 存档名为clawx_<tag>_windows_amd64.tar.gz。 在 PowerShell 中，使用匹配的 checksums.txt 下载它，验证 SHA256，并将clawx.exe 放入用户路径上的目录中：

$tag = "v0.2.1" # replace with the release tag you downloaded
$archive = "clawx_${tag}_windows_amd64.tar.gz"
$base = "https://github.com/debarshibasak/clawx/releases/download/$tag"

Invoke-WebRequest "$base/$archive" -OutFile ".\$archive"
Invoke-WebRequest "$base/checksums.txt" -OutFile .\checksums.txt
$expected = Get-Content .\checksums.txt |
  Where-Object { $_ -match "\s$([regex]::Escape($archive))$" } |
  ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "\s+")[0] } |
  Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $expected) { throw "No checksum found for $archive" }
$actual = (Get-FileHash ".\$archive" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected.ToLowerInvariant()) { throw "SHA256 verification failed" }

tar -xzf ".\$archive"
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $installDir | Out-Null
Move-Item -Force .\clawx.exe (Join-Path $installDir "clawx.exe")
$userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
$pathEntries = @($userPath -split ";" | Where-Object { $_ })
if ($pathEntries -notcontains $installDir) {
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", (($pathEntries + $installDir) -join ";"), "User")
}
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"
clawx --help

PowerShell 将 Clawx 状态存储在 %USERPROFILE%\.clawx 下（相当于 macOS/Linux 上的 ~/.clawx）。 当 stdout 是终端并回退到 more 时，clawx list 使用 $env:PAGER；使用clawx list --no-pager 或设置$env:CLAWX_NO_PAGER = "1" 进行非交互式输出。

WSL 是一个单独的环境：Linux Clawx 二进制文件使用 Linux 主目录 (~/.clawx) 和 Linux 提供程序 CLI。 从 PowerShell 启动的 Windows 二进制文件使用 %USERPROFILE%\.clawx 并需要在 Windows 路径上选择选定的提供程序 CLI；这两个环境不会自动共享状态。

或者从源代码构建：

go build -o clawx .      # or: make build
go install .             # or: make install

Clawx shells 为代理 CLI，因此您的 PATH 上需要 claude、codex、opencode、gemini 或 agy 之一。 默认是克劳德；使用 CLAWX_PROVIDER 选择另一个。

外壳完成

完成命令由 Cobra 生成。 安装clawx后，使用下面的shell设置并启动一个新shell（或获取生成的文件）以启用制表符完成。

Bash

对于 bash-completion v2，将生成的函数安装在用户完成目录中：

mkdir -p "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}"
clawx completion bash > "${BASH_COMPLETION_USER_DIR:-$HOME/.local/share/bash-completion/completions}/clawx"

在没有 bash-completion 的系统上，请从 shell 启动中获取文件：

clawx completion bash > "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"
printf '\nsource "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"\n' >> "$HOME/.bashrc"
source "$HOME/.clawx-completion.bash"

Zsh

对于原生 macOS zsh，将补全函数保留在用户目录中并将该目录添加到 fpath：

mkdir -p "$HOME/.zsh/completions"
clawx completion zsh > "$HOME/.zsh/completions/_clawx"
printf '\nfpath=("$HOME/.zsh/completions" $fpath)\nautoload -Uz compinit && compinit\n' >> "$HOME/.zshrc"
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit

如果 zsh 与 Homebrew 一起安装，请使用其站点功能目录（Apple Silicon 上的 /opt/homebrew，Intel 上的 /usr/local）：

zsh_site="$(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions"
mkdir -p "$zsh_site"
clawx completion zsh > "$zsh_site/_clawx"
autoload -Uz compinit && compinit

Fish

Fish 在新 shell 中自动从此目录加载完成文件：

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/fish/completions"
clawx completion fish > "$HOME/.config/fish/completions/clawx.fish"

用crawx安装clawx

已经有爪子了吗？ 它以运行其他所有内容的方式更新自身 - 内置注册表附带一个 install-clawx 包，该包获取最新版本，验证其校验和并安装二进制文件：

clawx run install-clawx

与每次运行一样，它首先经过批准提示，然后将执行记录到 ~/.clawx/execution.log。

快速入门

Clawx 附带一个内置的默认注册表（该存储库的注册表/目录通过 GitHub raw 提供），因此无需设置即可使用：

clawx list                        # browse the catalog
clawx search docker               # find packages by name/description
clawx info go-modernize           # what would this package do?
clawx run go-modernize            # fetch, verify, approve, execute
clawx history                     # what has run on this machine?
clawx rolladice                   # what should I run next?

javax help 打印完整的指南——命令、包格式、安全模型、环境变量和本地状态。

观察包运行

默认情况下，运行会打印一个实时进度行——已用时间、待办事项完成情况和当前工具调用——否则保持安静：

⠹ claude · 12s · todos 1/4 · 3 tool calls · Bash: go vet ./...

传递 --verbose （或设置 CLAWX_VERBOSE=1）以流式传输代理的叙述、工具调用及其待办事项列表：

$ clawx run go-modernize --verbose

Baseline is green (build ✅, tests ✅). Auditing the source now.
→ Bash: go vet ./...
── todos ──
  [x] Establish build/test baseline
  [>] Audit for deprecated APIs
  [ ] Write MODERNIZE.md

代理的最终摘要仅以详细模式显示。

命令

命令 签名 Does
add javax add <url> [--服务器] [--名称] [--ref] 注册注册表：git repo（默认）或clawx HTTP 服务器。
list 爪列表 [--刷新] [--无寻呼机] 列出每个配置的注册表中的包，在打印到终端时通过 $PAGER 进行分页。
搜索 javax 搜索 <术语> [术语...] [--刷新] 按名称和描述搜索包；多个术语必须全部匹配。
run javax run <名称>[@version] [-p k=v] [--prompt] [--verbose] [-y] 获取、验证、批准、执行。 关键路径。 别名为 install。
info clawx 信息 <名称> [--无摘要] 包元数据，以及其功能的无工具代理摘要。
罗拉迪切 javax rolladice [--fast] [--dir] [--no-agent] [--limit] 扫描您的工作区和注册表，建议下一步安装什么。
卸载 javax 卸载 <名称> [-y] 从本地状态删除安装记录。
更新 爪爪更新[名称] 重新获取软件包，当 SHA 或版本更改时重新安装。
历史 Clawx 历史 [--限制] 重播 NDJSON 执行日志。
管道 javax 管道 <pipeline.yaml> [--dry-run] 按顺序执行包的多步骤管道。 javax run <file.yaml> 的作用相同。
服务器 javax 服务器 --dir <路径> [--端口] 运行注册表 HTTP 服务器。 index.yaml 是在请求​​时构建的。

克劳克斯·罗拉迪斯

掷骰子决定下一步要安装什么。 它扫描当前目录中的项目（生态系统清单）、库（从这些清单中解析出来）、容器（Dockerfile、compose、Kubernetes、Helm、devcontainer）和值得注意的文件（CI、IaC、构建、测试、lint、数据、文档）——然后将所有这些与您的注册表提供的目录进行匹配。

  Detected:
    [*] go                 go.mod (github.com/acme/svc)
    [*] dockerfile         Dockerfile
    [*] kubernetes         deploy/app.yaml
    [*] ci:github-actions  .github/workflows/ci.yml

  Roll:

    1. base-setup               v1.0.0     score 72
       Prepare a Go service repository with linting and CI
       - required by installed analytics
       - matches your workspace: go, ci
       clawx run base-setup

排名是确定性的，并且离线运行：已安装软件包的未满足依赖关系优先于基于已安装软件包构建的软件包，后者优先于工作空间信号和共享词汇表匹配。 然后将入围名单交给代理，代理解释选择 - 只读调用，不授予任何工具。

  • --fast 跳过工作区行走和代理，纯粹根据您已安装的内容进行排名。 它以毫秒为单位返回。
  • --no-agent 打印离线候选名单而不调用任何代理。

仅打开清单文件。 .env 文件和您的源文件按路径记录，并且永远不会被读取。

封装格式

YAML 前面的内容由 --- 分隔，后面是成为代理系统提示符的 Markdown 正文。 仅需要姓名。

---
name: setup-project
version: 1.0.0
description: Scaffold a new project directory
author: adaptive-scale
author_email: team@adaptive.live
allowed_tools:
  - bash
env_required: []
depends_on: []
params:
  - name: project_name
    type: string          # string | int | bool
    required: true
    description: Directory to create
  - name: language
    type: string
    required: false
    default: go
---

You are a project scaffolding assistant. Use the Input Parameters provided to…

dependents_on 包以传递方式解析并首先以非交互方式安装。 夹具位于 testdata/packages/ 中。

想写一篇吗？ 在五分钟内创建您的第一个 Clawx 包，通过模板→本地测试→拉取请求，并附上真实的成绩单。

添加自定义注册表

  • git（默认）-clawx add github.com/owner/repo [--ref main]。 存储库克隆到 ~/.clawx/cache/repos/ 下，索引是根据其 *.md 文件构建的。
  • 服务器-crawx添加http://host:8080--server。 任何crawx服务器实例，它通过在请求时扫描其--dir来构建index.yaml。

要针对捆绑的固定装置尝试服务器风格：

./clawx server --dir ./testdata/packages --port 8080   # terminal 1

./clawx add http://localhost:8080 --server             # terminal 2
./clawx list
./clawx run hello-world

索引以 TTL（默认 1h）缓存在磁盘上； --refresh 绕过它。 使用 CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1 选择退出内置默认注册表。

供应商

代理 CLI 位于由 CLAWX_PROVIDER 选择的提供程序接口后面。

提供者 祈求 允许的工具
克劳德（默认） --系统提示文件 <tmp> 转发为 --allowedTools — 在子进程边界强制执行。
codex codex exec -，通过 stdin 提示 未转发；由 Codex 自己的批准/沙盒模式管理。
开放代码 opencode 运行，通过 stdin 提示 未转发；由 OpenCode 自己的配置管理。
双子座 系统提示符通过 GEMINI_SYSTEM_MD=<tmp>，用户提示符通过 -p 未转发；由 Gemini CLI 的批准模式和设置管理。
agy agy -p <提示>（反重力 CLI；别名：反重力） 未转发；由 agy 自己的许可提示管理。

这就是本自述文件顶部警告的不对称性： allowed_tools 是仅在 claude 下的真正安全边界。 在其他地方，它都是在批准提示中显示的披露。

clawx info 和clawx rolladice 是例外 - 两者都是只读调用，其系统提示禁止工具使用，并且在 claude 下根本没有传递 --allowedTools 标志。

环境

多变的 影响
CLAWX_PROVIDER 代理 CLI：claude（默认）、codex、opencode、gemini、agy。
CLAWX_PROVIDER_BIN 代理二进制文件的绝对路径，绕过 PATH 查找。
CLAWX_NO_DEFAULT_REGISTRY=1 不要注入内置的默认注册表。
CLAWX_INSTALL_IDS=1 每次安装生成并保留一个 UUID。
CLAWX_VERBOSE=1 流代理输出就像传递了 --verbose 一样。
CLAWX_NO_PAGER=1 切勿分页clawx列表输出，即使在终端上也是如此。
PAGER 由clawx列表使用的寻呼机（默认：先少-FRX，然后多）。

当地州

一切都保留在 ~/.clawx/ 下：

config.json        registries + cache TTL
cache/<sha>.json   cached registry indexes
cache/repos/       cloned git-backed registries
installed.json     install records
execution.log      NDJSON execution history

贡献

最简单的贡献不需要阅读任何 Go：编写一个包。 首先在五分钟内创建您的第一个 Clawx 包，然后查看良好的第一期标签。 CONTRIBUTING.md 涵盖了代码库本身，docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 解释了各个部分如何配合，而 ROADMAP.md 是项目的发展方向。 安全报告通过 SECURITY.md 进行。
